PullRequest.Title: [4/4] authentication: enable multiple configured enterprise hosts
PullRequest.Body:
## Review stack

**#338149 (merged) -> #338150 (merged) -> #338151 (merged) -> #338080 (multi-host enablement)**

This final layer targets `main`, building on the landed session-provenance API (#337846), distro enablement (#337882), provider lifecycle (#338150), and canonical credential storage (#338151). Part of #277435.

## Multi-host authentication

- Add unordered `github-enterprise.uris`, taking precedence over deprecated `github-enterprise.uri`, including explicit `[]`. No first-host default.
- Keep one `github-enterprise` provider and a separate public `github` provider. Return all eligible sessions, filtering scopes, account and issuer inside the provider/host engine.
- Preserve native session and account IDs. There are no host prefixes or ID-unwrapping transformations; `authorizationServer` remains the session's provenance.
- Construct session/account presentation in the host engine rather than rewriting every result/event in the facade. Enterprise account labels always use `username - host`, under the stable `GitHub Enterprise` provider label, even with one configured host. Ports and deployment paths remain visible when present.
- Keep account labels stable as other hosts are added or removed. There is no mutable suffix setter, cached relabeling pass, or host-count presentation flag. Native IDs and stored usernames remain unchanged.
- Resolve sign-in through explicit issuer/account hints, the sole host, or the extension-owned native picker. Preserve cancellation and platform preferences, permissions, silent/passive behavior and complete candidate lists.
- Remove a native session ID through cached ownership. In the rare case that the same session ID belongs to multiple hosts, report ambiguity instead of selecting an arbitrary host.

## Copilot enrollment

Copilot setup and onboarding accept **GHE.com instance names or HTTPS GHE.com URLs only**. General GitHub Enterprise authentication and configured-host validation still support GHES.

Invalid configured URI entries are prefilled for correction, one at a time, without replacing unrelated hosts. If only GHES is configured, Copilot enrollment prompts for a cloud instance and retains the existing server. Cancellation does not save the current prompt's proposed correction or start authentication.

The browser product-default fallback uses `github-enterprise.uri`, not an empty setting key. The prior Linux, macOS and Windows Browser CI failures were fixed and all three Browser jobs passed in run `36638660666`; that old run's remaining failure was unrelated WSL preparation/cleanup in Windows Electron-Smoke.

## Storage and compatibility

Canonical URI-derived credential storage comes from #338151: no storage-key registry or migration-completion flag. The temporary legacy migration remains marked for removal in 1.144, four releases after 1.140.

Legacy keys omitted the scheme. Ambiguous HTTP/HTTPS ownership requires an explicit original instance when migration is needed; already-authoritative canonical credentials are preserved. Native tokens and Microsoft account-link usernames remain intact.

The platform-wide structured-account identity migration remains deferred. This update may require one explicit account selection/consent for the new enterprise display labels. Adding or removing other hosts no longer changes an existing account's label. GitHub Pull Requests and GitHub Repositories should adopt session-derived routing before broad rollout.

## Latest validation

Rebased onto `origin/main` at `c46161fa184`, including the Microsoft sign-in probe from #338823. Current head: `a3f9a6f0af8`.

The onboarding conflict resolution preserves both the new Microsoft probe service/button behavior and trust-aware multi-host enrollment. The remaining commits replayed without conflicts; range-diff confirms no unrelated patch changes.

| Area | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Authentication extension, persistence and Microsoft broker/probe tests | **206 passing** |
| Core authentication RPC/selection, with native colliding account IDs | **66 passing** |
| Enrollment, parser, setup and onboarding in Chromium | **70 passing** |
| Enrollment, parser, setup and onboarding in WebKit | **70 passing** |
| Microsoft probe and external sign-in regressions | **23 passing in each of Chromium and WebKit** |

All counts are fresh runs after the rebase. Core and extension output was refreshed. Core and extension-browser type checks, scoped lint/hygiene and diff checks passed. Tests use fake services and isolated profiles, not user credentials. No fixture baselines, timeout thresholds, provider-level silent ambiguity policy, or test-only production APIs were added.

## Remaining validation

- [ ] Live sign-in/account switching across two real enterprise instances, including relevant brokered-account scenarios.
- [ ] Confirm downstream consumer releases are ready for rollout.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed critical path and boundary calls are directly traced in production code, and brokered sessions are explicitly transient while account links persist, making cold-window restoration repeatable. The number of users with multiple linked enterprise accounts is uncertain, which limits severity rather than confidence in the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Microsoft authentication IPC calls and GitHub token-exchange/user-info network requests
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On a cold window, work grows with the total remembered Microsoft-linked accounts across all newly configured hosts: each missing linked account performs Microsoft account/token lookups plus a GitHub token-exchange POST and user-info GET, while the outer Promise.all fans this out across hosts and waits for the slowest request.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Enterprise authentication provider registration and extension activation are blocked by the slowest configured host, with a concurrent network burst and potentially long startup/authentication latency when any secondary host is slow or unreachable.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, initialization could configure only one enterprise host, so at most that host's linked accounts were restored before registration; an unrelated secondary host could not add requests or hold the provider registration barrier open.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new multi-host initialization calls the full restoring getSessions path for every newly created host in parallel and does not commit/register the provider until all calls complete.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 87 changes startup from one awaited host engine to `Promise.all` over every `created` host and places all of their restoring session reads before `commitHosts`/provider registration.
Findings.Title: Register hosts before restoring every brokered session
Findings.Impact: After a reload with multiple configured GHE.com hosts and remembered Microsoft-brokered accounts, opening or using enterprise authentication waits for restoration on every host. One unreachable secondary host can therefore delay all otherwise usable enterprise accounts, while N hosts/accounts issue token-acquisition and GitHub exchange requests concurrently.
Findings.Evidence: `applyConfiguration` awaits `Promise.all(created.map(host => host.engine.getSessions(...)))` before `commitHosts` registers the provider. `GitHubSessionEngine.getSessions` calls `restore`; with a fresh engine, brokered sessions are absent because they are process-only, so each persisted account link enters `restoreOne`. `restoreNow` calls Microsoft account discovery and `renewWithMicrosoft`; `EntraTokenExchange.renew` silently acquires a Microsoft token, POSTs the token exchange, then GETs `/user` to verify identity. The engine coalesces only the same account/scope key, and the provider adds an outer all-host Promise.all, so distinct host/account work is neither bounded nor removed from the registration critical path.
Findings.Recommendation: Commit/register hosts from `getCachedSessions()` first, then restore brokered sessions after registration with bounded concurrency and forward the resulting session events; at minimum, avoid making one host's restoration a barrier for all hosts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold extension activation or configuration refresh with multiple enterprise hosts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Activation awaits configuration parsing, every new-host migration, engine credential loading, and every new engine's full `getSessions` restoration before `commitHosts` registers the enterprise provider. The reported brokered-session network work is therefore on the activation/provider-availability critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate all secret-storage keys for legacy migration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per newly added host; on cold activation H serialized calls, each main-thread call scans all machine secret keys before filtering to this extension.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only one enterprise URI was supported, so activation performed at most one enumeration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before host engines are created and before enterprise provider registration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read canonical host credentials from secret storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one read per created host, plus matching legacy-source reads only during migration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One enterprise engine performed one canonical credential read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each engine's persisted-session promise must settle before its initial session result completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List Microsoft accounts and silently acquire a Microsoft token
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per missing linked account on a cold window, subject to per-account/scope in-flight coalescing within one host only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the single configured enterprise host's linked accounts could enter this barrier.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by initial `getSessions`, therefore blocks provider registration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Exchange an Entra token for a GitHub token and fetch `/user` to verify identity
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two GitHub requests per restorable linked account, fanned out across all newly created hosts/accounts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: At most one host contributed this network restoration work and an unrelated secondary host could not delay registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The all-host barrier waits for the slowest exchange/user lookup before registration.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H distinct configured hosts after URI-key deduplication, S machine secret keys scanned by migration, and L total remembered Microsoft-linked accounts lacking process-local sessions across those hosts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Host migrations run serially. Engine initialization then uses an outer `Promise.all` across hosts; each engine uses another `Promise.all` across missing linked accounts, with only same host/account/scope requests coalesced and no aggregate limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Canonical persisted sessions are read once per engine and then cached. Microsoft-brokered sessions are intentionally process-only, so every cold window starts with misses; successful restores populate transient sessions, failed restore keys are negatively cached only for that engine lifetime, and concurrent identical restores coalesce.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the cold-cache condition, nested Promise.all fan-out, network calls, and pre-registration await are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Multiple configured hosts are the feature target, but the prevalence of remembered Microsoft-linked accounts on more than one GHE.com host and actual endpoint latency are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable materially amplified startup boundary fan-out: one finding submitted for registering only after all hosts restore brokered sessions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Routine enterprise session enumeration for account menus and extension authentication requests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A request without account or issuer hints awaits every configured host; issuer/account-resolved requests use one host. Persisted and already-restored sessions are local after engine initialization, while an unresolved cold brokered link performs restoration before the request returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Renew or restore Microsoft-brokered GitHub sessions when no matching warm session exists
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero on the normal warm persisted path; on misses, one renewal flow per distinct stale session or missing account/scope key after coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Broad enterprise enumeration reached only the one configured host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Requests requiring the missing session await renewal/restoration; broad unhinted enumeration can await all hosts.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H configured hosts, sessions per host, and any linked accounts not already represented by a matching session; URI keys deduplicate equivalent configured entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unresolved requests use `Promise.all` across hosts. Per-engine renewals/restores coalesce by session or account/scope key, but distinct hosts/accounts run concurrently without a shared limiter. Ext-host provider operations serialize calls for the provider.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persisted-session promises and transient sessions make normal warm enumeration local. Restore failures are negatively cached for the engine lifetime and successes suppress later restoration for that account/scope. A window reload clears transient/negative caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for routing and cache behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most warm reads perform no network work; frequency depends on callers and brokered-session use.
Scenarios.Verdict: The cold all-host cost is covered by the activation finding. Warm fan-out is predominantly local and returning all configured hosts is required, so no additional finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive enterprise sign-in and session removal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Sign-in resolves an issuer/account hint or waits for the native host picker, then only the selected host's interactive login/token/user-info path runs. Removal scans already-loaded host caches, then logs out and updates credentials on the single owning host.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Selected-host OAuth/Microsoft sign-in, user lookup, or logout
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The sole configured host performed the same interactive boundary work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Expected interactive authentication work; no unrelated host network request is added.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/write the selected host's secret storage entry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One canonical entry for the selected host, with extension-wide change notifications causing low-frequency cache reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Credential persistence and reconciliation already occurred for the single enterprise engine.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Credential persistence is awaited; unrelated-host reconciliation is off the direct interactive return path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H configured hosts for local ownership scans; one selected host and one session for interactive boundary work. Ambiguous native IDs stop before logout.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Host ownership cache checks are sequential for removal/account resolution but are local after initialization. Interactive authentication and logout target one engine; no per-host network fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Host ownership uses each engine's persisted/transient cache. Sign-in writes one host's canonical secret, and secret-change listeners may trigger additional per-engine cache reads, but token changes are infrequent and the added cost is not independently significant enough to report.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of configured hosts affects only cheap local scans here; sign-in/removal frequency is user-driven and low.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate performance regression: expensive work remains constrained to one selected/owning host.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot enterprise enrollment and onboarding correction
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The UI reads effective configuration, validates the finite URI list, optionally waits for one user input at a time, writes one configuration value, then starts the existing setup/sign-in flow. Validation and list scans are synchronous local work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one settings write per accepted correction/enrollment input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Enrollment wrote the single legacy URI setting once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before authentication setup so the provider sees the new host; not multiplied per existing valid host.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of configured URI strings and invalid entries; realistic lists are small and each correction removes one invalid entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Corrections are intentionally sequential user interactions. There is no subprocess, IPC burst, database, filesystem, or network loop in URI validation; one configuration update is awaited per accepted correction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration is re-read before each write to preserve concurrent additions. No long-lived cache or negative-cache state is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: URI arrays are user-configured but expected to remain small; no expensive operation scales with every valid host.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; added scans are bounded local validation and configuration work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all changed files and traced activation, migration, session enumeration/restoration, interactive authentication, removal, trust/configuration refresh, and enrollment. Submitted one medium-confidence-severity startup finding for the new all-host brokered-session restoration barrier; other added multiplicity is local, cached, low-frequency, or required and bounded.
